court: Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

issues.label: Jurisdiction and standard of review
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction and apply the correct standards for reviewing legal questions, factual findings, and credibility determinations.

issues.label: Timeliness of asylum application
issues.why: Eligibility for asylum requires a timely filing or a valid exception, even if the agency or parties said it was timely.

issues.label: Asylum statutory eligibility
issues.why: The court must determine whether the facts, if credited, satisfy the definition of “refugee” under the INA.

issues.label: Nexus to protected ground
issues.why: Relief requires persecution “on account of” political opinion (actual or imputed) or other protected grounds.

issues.label: Political opinion characterization
issues.why: The court must assess whether UNITA/PRA-JA activism and denunciation of abuses constitute protected political opinion.

issues.label: Past persecution threshold
issues.why: The court must decide whether the alleged beatings, detention, and threats rise to “persecution” severity.

issues.label: State actor involvement
issues.why: Because harm is attributed to police/military, the court must treat it as government persecution/torture rather than private violence.

issues.label: Well-founded fear of future persecution
issues.why: If asylum credibility or past persecution fails, the court must still evaluate future fear based on record evidence.

issues.label: Presumption from past persecution
issues.why: If past persecution is established, a regulatory presumption of future persecution applies and must be properly rebutted.

issues.label: Government rebuttal burden
issues.why: Rebuttal requires showing changed conditions or safe internal relocation, with the correct burden allocation.

issues.label: Internal relocation reasonableness
issues.why: The court must assess both feasibility and reasonableness of relocating within Angola under governing factors.

issues.label: Relocation burden allocation
issues.why: When persecutor is the government, DHS bears the burden to show internal relocation is reasonable and safe.

issues.label: Changed country conditions
issues.why: The court must consider whether conditions in Angola materially changed to reduce risk to the applicant.

issues.label: Withholding of removal standard
issues.why: The court must separately apply the “more likely than not” persecution standard for withholding.

issues.label: Withholding nexus standard
issues.why: Withholding requires a protected ground to be “a reason” (not necessarily central), which must be applied correctly.

issues.label: Separate analysis for each relief
issues.why: The agency must not conflate asylum, withholding, and CAT standards; each requires distinct findings.

issues.label: Adverse credibility legal standard
issues.why: The court must ensure the IJ/BIA applied the REAL ID Act credibility framework and proper legal criteria.

issues.label: Specific, cogent credibility reasons
issues.why: An adverse credibility finding must rest on specific reasons supported by substantial evidence.

issues.label: Each credibility ground validity
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether each of the four cited credibility grounds is supported and material.

issues.label: Totality-of-circumstances credibility
issues.why: The court must ensure the agency considered the totality, not isolated discrepancies, when assessing credibility.

issues.label: Materiality of inconsistencies
issues.why: Even if minor inconsistencies may be considered, the court must decide whether reliance was reasonable and supported.

issues.label: Opportunity to explain discrepancies
issues.why: Due process and credibility rules require giving the applicant a fair chance to explain perceived inconsistencies.

issues.label: Corroboration requirements
issues.why: The court must check whether the IJ properly applied corroboration rules (availability, notice, and reasonableness).

issues.label: Corroboration notice and findings
issues.why: If corroboration was required, the IJ must identify what evidence was expected and whether it was reasonably obtainable.

issues.label: Weight to corroborating evidence
issues.why: The court must assess whether the IJ/BIA properly evaluated documentary/medical/affidavit evidence for rehabilitation.

issues.label: Failure of spouse to testify
issues.why: The court must consider whether drawing inferences from the wife’s non-testimony was permissible and procedurally fair.

issues.label: Pro se hearing fairness
issues.why: Because the applicant appeared pro se, the court must consider whether the IJ adequately developed the record.

issues.label: Interpreter/communication adequacy
issues.why: If language issues existed or were alleged, the court must ensure interpretation did not undermine fairness or accuracy.

issues.label: Trauma and memory effects
issues.why: The court must consider whether trauma or detention could reasonably affect recall, impacting credibility assessment.

issues.label: Persecution vs lawful prosecution
issues.why: The court must distinguish persecution for political opinion from legitimate law enforcement actions at rallies.

issues.label: Mixed motives analysis
issues.why: If authorities had multiple motives (crowd control vs politics), the court must apply correct mixed-motive standards.

issues.label: Pattern or practice claim
issues.why: The court must consider whether there is a pattern or practice of persecuting opposition activists in Angola.

issues.label: Imputed political opinion risk
issues.why: Risk may stem from authorities imputing opposition affiliation due to rally participation and denunciation.

issues.label: Fear based on whistleblowing
issues.why: Publicly denouncing a detainee’s death may be political expression or perceived opposition triggering retaliation.

issues.label: Threats as persecution
issues.why: The court must determine whether death threats and pursuit by military constitute persecution or contribute cumulatively.

issues.label: Cumulative harm assessment
issues.why: The court must assess all incidents together rather than in isolation to determine persecution/torture likelihood.

issues.label: CAT legal standard
issues.why: CAT requires showing it is more likely than not the applicant would be tortured if removed.

issues.label: Definition of torture
issues.why: The court must apply the regulatory definition (severe pain/suffering, intent, purpose) to the alleged abuse.

issues.label: Government acquiescence element
issues.why: CAT requires torture by or with consent/acquiescence of officials, which is implicated by police/military conduct.

issues.label: CAT independent of credibility
issues.why: Even with adverse credibility, the agency must evaluate whether objective evidence independently establishes CAT risk.

issues.label: Particularized risk requirement
issues.why: The court must decide whether the record shows a personal, individualized risk rather than generalized violence.

issues.label: CAT country conditions evidence
issues.why: The court must consider whether reports on Angola show torture risks for opposition activists/detainees.

issues.label: CAT internal relocation relevance
issues.why: The court must address whether relocation meaningfully reduces torture likelihood and how it factors into CAT analysis.

issues.label: Past torture consideration
issues.why: Prior torture is a key factor in CAT likelihood and must be weighed even if asylum is denied.

issues.label: Agency reasoning adequacy (CAT)
issues.why: The court must ensure the IJ/BIA provided reasoned consideration rather than denying CAT solely on credibility.

issues.label: BIA adoption/affirmance clarity
issues.why: The court must determine which IJ findings the BIA adopted and whether any issues were independently analyzed.

issues.label: Exhaustion of administrative remedies
issues.why: Claims not raised to the BIA may be unexhausted and outside the court’s review authority.

issues.label: Issue preservation and waiver
issues.why: The court must identify arguments waived by not briefing them adequately on appeal to the court or BIA.

issues.label: Due process: full and fair hearing
issues.why: The court must decide whether procedural defects denied a meaningful opportunity to present the case.

issues.label: Due process: IJ bias or conduct
issues.why: If alleged, the court must assess whether IJ behavior compromised neutrality or record development.

issues.label: Due process: notice and opportunity
issues.why: The court must assess whether the applicant had notice of evidentiary needs and a chance to respond.

issues.label: Prejudice requirement
issues.why: Due process relief requires showing the outcome may have been affected by the alleged violation.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: Even if error occurred, the court must decide whether it was harmless given the overall record.

issues.label: Derivative asylum for family
issues.why: If the principal qualifies for asylum, the court must consider derivative eligibility for spouse/children.

issues.label: Family member independent claims
issues.why: The court must consider whether any family member has an independent basis for relief if raised or supported.

issues.label: Country of removal designation
issues.why: Relief analyses must be tied to the specific country of removal (Angola) and any alternative designations.

issues.label: Eligibility bars to asylum/withholding
issues.why: The court must ensure no statutory bars apply (e.g., serious crime, persecutor bar), even if not prominent in the record.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocations
issues.why: The court must confirm the correct burdens for asylum, withholding, CAT, and relocation were applied.

issues.label: Substantial evidence review constraints
issues.why: The court must respect the agency’s factfinding unless compelled to conclude otherwise under the record.

issues.label: Remand vs reversal scope
issues.why: If error is found, the court must decide whether to remand for further findings or grant relief outright.
